title: Cryptographically verifiable WORM audit evidence pipeline for admin/config actions
creator: Marina Zhou
description: Background: Enterprises need provable, tamper-evident audit evidence for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes to satisfy auditors and data residency/retention requirements. Current audit sinks capture events but lack an end-to-end verifiable chain and cross-region retention enforcement. Goal: Build an append-only evidence pipeline that writes signed, immutable records to a WORM-backed storage layer (S3 Object Lock / on-prem equivalent), generates periodic cryptographic attestations (Merkle roots + HSM-signed timestamps), enforces retention and legal-hold policies per customer data residency, and exposes automated export/reporting endpoints for compliance teams and auditors.
acceptance_criteria: All admin actions, RBAC changes, and config updates are emitted to the new evidence pipeline with identical schema to existing audit logs
Evidence objects are written to a WORM-enabled store (S3 Object Lock or on-prem immutable store) with retention headers set per-customer policy
Each evidence batch is included in a Merkle tree; the pipeline publishes signed attestations (timestamp + root hash) to an append-only ledger and to a customer-visible endpoint
Exports for auditor requests (CSV and JSONL) are reproducible and include attestation metadata proving the exported records were present in the immutable store at the stated time
Cross-region retention rules respect customer data residency tags; pipeline prevents copying evidence outside allowed regions
End-to-end tests (unit + integration) and a baseline performance dashboard (latency, write throughput, storage growth) are present
Design and implementation pass security review and key management (KMS/HSM) audit
tasks: Define canonical evidence schema for admin/action/config events and map existing log sources
Prototype Merkle tree builder and attestation signer (HSM integration) - proof-of-concept service
Integrate WORM storage adapters: S3 Object Lock implementation and on-prem immutable store abstraction
Retention & legal-hold enforcement module: policy engine that applies per-customer rules and prevents premature deletion
Region-aware writer: ensure writes honor data_residency tag and enforce cross-region prohibitions
API endpoints for auditors: time-bound exports with attached attestations (CSV/JSONL) and checksum validation
Monitoring & alerting: metricize evidence write failures, attestation delays, and retention policy mismatches
Migration plan for backfilling recent 90-day audit records into WORM store for customers under active contracts
Performance testing and cost estimation for high-traffic tenants; provide quantized recommendations for Dedicated/Private
notes: Trade-offs: S3 Object Lock provides a convenient managed WORM solution in AWS, but for Private customers we must provide an appliance-compatible patterns (immutable filesystem + append-only index).

We chose Merkle trees + HSM signing to balance verifier simplicity (clients can fetch root + proof) and non-repudiation. Timestamping via an external trusted time service (RFC 3161/TSA) is planned for final attestation chain.
Retention enforcement will be handled at the storage adapter layer; upper layers will treat deletion attempts as signals for alerts/review rather than performing deletes directly.

Cost note: keeping all evidence indefinitely is not feasible; retention policies must default to conservative values (e.g., 7 years for regulated customers) with clear cost estimates surfaced in Console.
